    else:

The issue was that `Progress.stop()` was printing a blank line on non-interactive consoles even when `disable=True` was set. This happened because `Progress.start()` correctly checked `self.disable` before starting the `Live` display, but `Progress.stop()` did not perform the same check before calling `self.live.stop()` and printing the blank line.

I have updated `rich/progress.py` to wrap the contents of the `stop` method in an `if not self.disable:` block, making it symmetrical to the `start` method.

Verified the fix with a reproduction script that confirmed no output is produced when `disable=True` on a non-interactive console.
